pairs.why: B's truss rails, yoke and can keep thin straight runs and tight edges like the real fixture, while A fattens the truss into a toy with capsule end caps.
A keeps a flat rectangular back panel between thin tube posts, like the real chair's flat strip on a tube frame, while B's back is a wavy, pillowed shape.
B's star is flatter, with straight edges and crisper points, while A's is a swollen pillow with a puffy face.
Neither rope drawing gives my vector a reason to choose, and the real cards show no rope to compare against.
A's frame and target are simpler and closer to the real cards' plain straight-run frame, while B has a wavy top and extra clutter (cans, ball, flag) that change the part count.
A's bottle body is slender and tapered like the real one, while B's is squat and swollen with a fat handle loop.
B has boxy cab faces, straight runs and thin pipes and rails, like the real cards' crisp planar forms, while A is a chunky toy shape with fat rounded parts.
B's thick-slab planks and stout posts are closer to the real chunky pier, while A's posts are tall and thin, but the difference is slight.
